title: The channel rotation in the Askey scheme: same eigenfunctions rotated, different measures
html:
The bar-even (binding, \cosh) and bar-odd (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta, \sinh) channels of the complex volume \mathfrak{V} constitute a single Askey-scheme family evaluated through a rotation. Both the rotation and its limits are classical.

Channel recurrences

The continuous q-Hermite polynomials H_n(x \mid q) construct the proved basis of the binding kernel. Under simultaneous variable rotation x \mapsto ix and bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1}, they yield the Ismail–Masson q^{-1}-Hermite polynomials:

h_n(x \mid q) \;=\; i^{-n}\, H_n(ix \mid q^{-1}).

The two channel recurrences are identical up to this rotation. We formalize this generically over a commutative ring R equipped with a bar involution \sigma and a formal rotation element \iota satisfying \iota^2 = -1. The Lean declaration rotation_step (sibling to conj:binding-qbeta-complex-volume) encodes this: a sequence satisfies the odd-channel step at (q, x) if and only if its \iota-rotation satisfies the even-channel step at (\sigma q, \iota x). The archimedean i emerges only downstream of the functor \tau.

Orthogonality measures

The shared recurrence does not imply a shared spectral measure. The asymmetry remains structural:

even channel (binding) odd channel (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta)
polynomials H_n(x \mid q), x = \cos\theta h_n(x \mid q), x = \sinh t
locus compact, x \in [-1, 1] non-compact, x \in \mathbb{R}
measure q-Plancherel weight (determinate) indeterminate moment problem
at q_0 > 1 does not exist archimedeanly native regime

At the substrate anchor q_0 > 1, the even-channel measure fails to form a probability law (prop:q-gaussian-obstruction-at-q0). This presents the Bożejko–Speicher positivity obstruction. The rotation is therefore irreducibly fibre-level, consistent with observable \mathrm{Im}(q_0) = 0. Measure asymmetry explains why parity projection left the binding error unchanged while the recurrence tie holds. A three-term recurrence is measure-independent, whereas a projection is not.

Literature precedents

  1. Askey and Ismail–Masson: The q > 1 continuation of continuous q-Hermite [askey1989qhermite] provides the eigenfunction rotation [ismail-masson1994].
  2. The modular double: The non-compact channel couples q = e^{i\pi b^2} to \tilde{q} = e^{-i\pi/b^2}. Ponsot–Teschner Racah–Wigner coefficients for U_q(\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})) [ponsot-teschner2001] sit at the non-compact Askey–Wilson level. The map b \leftrightarrow 1/b drives the 6j-level rotation: the self-dual representations of U_q are automatically U_{\tilde q}-representations \cite[\S2.1, \S2.3]{terashima-yamazaki2013}. That source writes \tilde q = e^{+i\pi/b^2}, the complex conjugate of the \tilde q above. This divides \Phi_q (Faddeev, non-compact) from \mathrm{Li}_2^q (Rogers, compact).
  3. Quantum modularity: The Andersen–Kashaev state integral of a knot factors into a q-series and a \tilde{q}-series. The leading asymptotics trace \mathrm{Vol} + i\,\mathrm{CS} [garoufalidis-zagier-2024]. One complex object dictates two channel factorizations, mirroring the Neumann–Zagier structure [neumann-zagier1985] that \mathfrak{V} transports to binding and decay.

Leonard pairs

Zhedanov's AW(3) algebra [zhedanov1991] embeds the rotation as an operator identity. It pairs two operators, each tridiagonal in the other's eigenbasis, with Askey–Wilson polynomials forming the overlap matrix. The generic statement—that any eigencolumn of the channel tridiagonal operator has orthogonal-polynomial entries—is proved as eigencolumn_eq_overlap. The self-duality that places the channel overlap into the Askey–Wilson family via Terwilliger's classification [terwilliger2001] is axiomatized by the conjecture class ChannelLeonardDuality.

Vertex-algebra shadow

Under the bar involution, the character side splits as a \mathbb{Z}_2-orbifold V = V^+ \oplus V^-. The involved characters form false theta functions, appearing as (1,p) singlet log-VOA characters [creutzig-milas2014]. Their quantum modularity tracks the disk-interior versus root-of-unity rotation, using the Lawrence–Zagier \Psi operation established for W_\lambda. This structure suggests a path to unify the lepton-tower \Phi_q mechanism with the binding/decay model.
